[{"order_index":1,"outcome":"Write C++ programs that read from standard input, write to standard output, and use fundamental data types including int, long long, double, char, and string for basic computation tasks.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/io"},"rationale":"Input/output operations and type systems form the foundation of every competitive programming solution. Without mastery of these, learners cannot read problem constraints, process test data, or produce correctly formatted output.","stable_id":"cpp-io-types","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can read two integers, compute a result, and print the output correctly for AtCoder ABC practice problem 1 without consulting references.","title":"C++ I/O and types"},{"order_index":2,"outcome":"Implement C++ programs using conditional statements including if/else and switch, loops including for and while, and custom functions with parameters and return values to control program execution flow.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/statements"},"rationale":"Control flow and functions are the building blocks of algorithmic thinking. Conditionals model decision logic, loops handle repetition, and functions encapsulate reusable computation patterns essential for any non-trivial problem.","stable_id":"cpp-control-flow-functions","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can write a function that processes an array with a loop, uses conditionals for branching, and passes all test cases for ABC086 A Product without external help.","title":"C++ control flow and functions"},{"order_index":3,"outcome":"Select and apply standard C++ containers including vector, string, and array to store, access, and manipulate ordered collections of data in algorithmic problem solving.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector"},"rationale":"Standard library containers eliminate manual memory management and provide battle-tested data structures. Understanding when to use vector versus array versus string directly determines whether a solution is correct and efficient.","stable_id":"cpp-containers","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can choose the appropriate container for a problem, iterate over elements with range-based for loops, and solve ABC081 B Shift Only independently.","title":"C++ containers"},{"order_index":4,"outcome":"Decompose programming problems into smaller reusable functions and modules, applying separation of concerns to build maintainable solutions with clear interfaces and testable components.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/functions"},"rationale":"Large problems cannot be solved in a single monolithic block of code. Decomposition into smaller, testable functions reduces cognitive load, enables parallel debugging, and is the prerequisite skill for all advanced algorithm design.","stable_id":"program-decomposition","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can break down a problem into three or more cooperating functions, define clear parameter contracts, and solve ABC085 C Otoshidama without looking at solutions.","title":"Program decomposition"},{"order_index":5,"outcome":"Diagnose and fix common C++ bugs using systematic debugging techniques including breakpoints, print-based tracing, and structured test case construction with boundary analysis.","provenance":{"authority":"GNU Project","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html"},"rationale":"Even experienced programmers spend more time debugging than writing code. Systematic debugging with tools and structured test cases transforms frustrating guesswork into a repeatable engineering discipline.","stable_id":"debugging-testing","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can reproduce a failing test case from output alone, identify the logical error through systematic debugging, and correct it for ARC065 A Daydream.","title":"Debugging and testing"},{"order_index":6,"outcome":"Initialize Git repositories, stage and commit changes with meaningful messages, and compile C++ programs using command-line build tools in a reproducible development workflow.","provenance":{"authority":"Git SCM","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Getting-a-Git-Repository"},"rationale":"Version control and reproducible builds are non-negotiable professional skills. Git protects against lost work and enables experimentation, while command-line compilation removes IDE dependency for consistent results.","stable_id":"git-build-workflow","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can initialize a Git repository, commit changes with descriptive messages, compile a multi-file C++ program, and explain the build pipeline to another learner.","title":"Git and build workflow"},{"order_index":7,"outcome":"Analyze the time and space complexity of algorithms using Big-O notation, estimate worst-case behavior from nested loops and recursive calls, and justify efficiency trade-offs between competing approaches.","provenance":{"authority":"OI Wiki","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://oi-wiki.org/basic/complexity/"},"rationale":"Algorithm complexity is the universal language for comparing solutions. Without Big-O analysis, learners cannot predict whether their code will run within time limits or choose between competing algorithmic approaches.","stable_id":"complexity-analysis","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can estimate the time complexity of a nested-loop solution to within one order of magnitude, predict whether it passes ABC constraints, and optimize accordingly.","title":"Complexity analysis"},{"order_index":8,"outcome":"Implement common sorting algorithms and binary search, apply C++ standard library sort and lower_bound functions, and solve problems requiring ordered data access patterns and efficient lookup.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/algorithm/lower_bound"},"rationale":"Sorting and binary search appear in the majority of intermediate competitive programming problems. The C++ standard library provides optimized implementations, but learners must understand when and how to apply them correctly.","stable_id":"sorting-binary-search","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can sort an array with std::sort, use lower_bound for binary search, and independently solve ARC084 A Snuke's Festival using the two approaches combined.","title":"Sorting and binary search"},{"order_index":9,"outcome":"Model and solve problems using stack with LIFO semantics and queue with FIFO semantics, including bracket matching, expression evaluation, and breadth-first traversal preparation tasks.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/queue"},"rationale":"Stacks and queues model real-world ordering constraints and appear as building blocks in graph traversal, expression parsing, and state management. Mastering them now prevents re-deriving these patterns during harder graph problems.","stable_id":"stacks-queues","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can recognize a stack or queue problem from its description, implement the solution with std::stack or std::queue, and solve ABC007 C without external references.","title":"Stacks and queues"},{"order_index":10,"outcome":"Apply hash-based containers including unordered_map and unordered_set for O(1) average-time lookups and implement linked-list traversal for problems requiring sequential pointer-based access patterns.","provenance":{"authority":"cppreference.com","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/unordered_map"},"rationale":"Hash tables provide amortized constant-time lookup that transforms quadratic-time nested loops into linear scans. Linked structures introduce pointer-based traversal, a fundamental pattern for trees and graphs ahead.","stable_id":"hashing-linked-structures","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can use unordered_map for frequency counting, detect duplicate removal with unordered_set, and solve ABC073 C Write and Erase using hash-based approaches.","title":"Hashing and linked structures"},{"order_index":11,"outcome":"Represent tree structures in C++, implement recursive and iterative depth-first traversals, and solve problems involving subtree queries, path sums, and ancestor relationships efficiently.","provenance":{"authority":"OI Wiki","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://oi-wiki.org/graph/dfs/"},"rationale":"Trees model hierarchical relationships found in file systems, organization charts, and parse trees. Recursive traversal is the essential mental model for divide-and-conquer algorithms and dynamic programming on trees.","stable_id":"trees-recursion-traversal","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can build a tree from parent or edge input, write a recursive DFS to aggregate subtree values, and solve ABC138 D Ki without consulting the editorial.","title":"Trees, recursion, and traversal"},{"order_index":12,"outcome":"Model problems as directed and undirected graphs, implement BFS for shortest-path and level-order traversal, and apply DFS for connectivity analysis, cycle detection, and topological exploration.","provenance":{"authority":"OI Wiki","retrieved_at":"2026-07-17T00:00:00.000Z","url":"https://oi-wiki.org/graph/bfs/"},"rationale":"Graphs are the most expressive data structure in computer science, modeling networks, dependencies, and state spaces. BFS and DFS together solve connectivity, shortest-path, and reachability problems throughout advanced competitive programming.","stable_id":"graphs-bfs-dfs","status":"published","stopping_guidance":"Stop when you can represent a graph with adjacency lists, run BFS for shortest-path queries on unweighted graphs, and independently solve ABC168 D using BFS traversal.","title":"Graphs: BFS and DFS"}]
